findings.body: These assertions do not isolate the launcher's environment. `review.py:316` sets FORGE_WORKER=1 on the outer close test run, `scripts/fast-test.py:38–39` preserves it, and `tests/conftest.py:159–161` launches Forge with the inherited environment; its repo fixture does not clear the marker. Consequently, during the supplied close-run validation, removing the explicit environment assignments from worker, reader or reviewer launchers would still satisfy every injected assertion. Clear or replace FORGE_WORKER in the parent test environment before invoking Forge, so each provider case proves Forge supplies it.
findings.title: Not done: prove every worker, reader and reviewer gets FORGE_WORKER=1

findings.body: The previous finding remains open. A successful initial answer can ask a question and leave uncommitted changes, but a failed commit nudge prevents `_question` from running. Both Claude paths leave `outcome` as failed when the nudge raises (lines 188–196); Codex explicitly changes it to failed when the nudge returns an unsuccessful status (lines 212–213). The initial question receives neither a pending record nor an occurrence id, allowing subsequent work or close to proceed unanswered: `close.py:64–66` blocks only persisted questions. Preserve questions from successful answers independently of the nudge outcome, across both Claude routes and Codex.
findings.title: Preserve pending questions when a commit nudge fails
